kata.name: Factory-method role-annotated fallback exclusion - a new kind served by the declared fallback with the creator map agreeing, caught by the role/policy equation on an unsampled kind
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md Factory Method row (disposed; construction dispatch); fixtures/katas/factory-method/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.2
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered (H2, committed before its fixtures were built): the agreement equation is satisfied and the role/policy equation emits an executed violation on the unsampled kind yaml (row 3); one unique element, scoped to the authored role classification (coverage-only)

expected.detail: yaml's arm is the fallback create_default and creator(yaml) also names create_default, so the agreement equation is satisfied; role(create_default) = fallback and expected_role(yaml) = concrete, so route;handler;role = expected_role emits an executed violation on the yaml row. The baseline sample is {json, text}

comparison.conventional_baseline: the scripted factory test over the pre-registered sample {json, text}; yaml is unsampled, so the fallback-served kind is invisible to it. A complete-domain conventional test would catch it, which is why the scope is coverage-only.

baseline.artifact: prototype/factory_method_baseline.py sha256:62553030b06c98d87d43bed081b1d857b2d41fb9d243d63bf17ee93e0cbf3848 (scripted sampled factory dispatch test; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: the fallback classification is derivable from the dispatch structure
expressibility_gap.why: it is not: the role arrow is authored data. gap-declared-fallback.ct.json and dispatch.ct.json share a model hash, so the structure cannot name a fallback; the role vocabulary must be declared

expressibility_gap.invariant: the expected role is per-kind expectation data
expressibility_gap.why: expected_role is a policy constant (every declared kind concrete). A document that declared expected_role = fallback for a kind would satisfy the equation, so the law checks the declared policy, not intent

expressibility_gap.invariant: the running binary's switch is the transcribed dispatch
expressibility_gap.why: the document is a transcription; nothing proves the executable's arm table matches it
